docs.title: Edd Straw's 2026 F1 Miami Grand Prix driver rankings

claims.claim: Alpine's qualifying pace advantage over rivals was several tenths of a second, which Lawson said caught out Racing Bulls and Bearman admitted was unexpected.

claims.quote: Cadillac choosing Saturday's race to run the hard tyres for the first time and gather data for the grand prix.

docs.title: Winners and losers from F1's 2026 Miami sprint

claims.quote: McLaren confirmed its sprint supremacy in Miami by breaking Mercedes’ unbeaten run and clinching its first 1-2 of 2026.
claims.claim: McLaren achieved its first 1-2 finish of the 2026 season in the Miami sprint, ending Mercedes' unbeaten run.

claims.quote: The second Lando Norris made it to the first corner in front, a fourth-career sprint victory never looked in doubt. He was simply in cruise control from start to finish and never came under any pressure to defend his lead
claims.claim: Lando Norris led from the first corner and won the Miami sprint without facing any pressure on his lead, which was his fourth career sprint victory.

claims.quote: Oscar Piastri, on the other hand, saw off some late pressure from Charles Leclerc to keep a firm grip of second place.
claims.claim: Oscar Piastri finished second in the Miami sprint after resisting late pressure from Charles Leclerc.

claims.quote: It began with a terrible start, and ended with a track limits penalty - Kimi Antonelli had a terrible sprint Saturday.
claims.claim: Kimi Antonelli suffered a poor start and received a track limits penalty during the Miami sprint.

claims.quote: Antonelli said he’d done all the procedures on the start correctly so that wasn’t his fault, but the many driving errors and track limits infringements thereafter made us think back to the rookie of a year ago
claims.claim: Antonelli claimed his poor start was not due to driver error, but he committed multiple driving errors and track limits infringements during the race.

claims.quote: Even Leclerc had a massive pop at Antonelli's “unbelievable” (in a bad way!) wheel-to-wheel combat, although Leclerc did soften those comments out of the cockpit afterwards.
claims.claim: Leclerc publicly criticised Antonelli's wheel-to-wheel racing during the sprint but later moderated his comments after the race.

claims.quote: Toto Wolff admitted the team was “hoping we were going to be able to hold onto our advantage” but never looked close to podium-level pace.
claims.claim: Toto Wolff acknowledged Mercedes hoped to maintain their advantage but the team lacked podium-level pace in the Miami sprint.

claims.quote: its chances of a top three finish were scuppered by its best candidate - that was Antonelli - with the poor race start and for picking up that needless track limits penalty which demoted him from fourth to sixth after the flag.
claims.claim: Antonelli was demoted from fourth to sixth place after the Miami sprint due to a post-race track limits penalty.

claims.quote: he was fortunate not to drop behind Max Verstappen at the chequered flag, with his pace seemingly evaporating in the latter stages as Mercedes’ winning streak came to a juddering end.
claims.claim: George Russell narrowly avoided being overtaken by Verstappen at the end of the Miami sprint as his pace faded in the closing stages.

claims.quote: There have been five competitive starts so far this season: three grands prix, and two sprint races. And Audi has failed to put one of its cars on the grid three times out of five.
claims.claim: Audi failed to start at least one car in three out of five competitive sessions in the 2026 season.

claims.quote: Nico Hulkenberg’s smoky exit on the reconnaissance laps marked yet another technical failure of some description for the new works team, which also only had one car take the start in the Australian and Chinese GPs.
claims.claim: Hulkenberg retired before the Miami sprint start due to a technical failure, and Audi had also fielded only one car at the Australian and Chinese Grands Prix.

claims.quote: Gabriel Bortoleto lost his 11th place after being disqualified by the stewards for an engine air intake pressure breach.
claims.claim: Gabriel Bortoleto was disqualified from 11th place in the Miami sprint for an engine air intake pressure regulation breach.

claims.quote: It got dicey on the opening lap sandwiched between Lewis Hamilton and Franco Colapinto, and contact with the latter, and the move on Hamilton mid-race that went just a touch too far led to a slightly laboured bit of letting the Ferrari back through.
claims.claim: Verstappen made contact with Colapinto on the opening lap, and a mid-race move on Hamilton resulted in Verstappen having to give the position back to the Ferrari.

claims.quote: his race ended on such a high that he was able to beat the penalised Antonelli by a tenth of a second!
claims.claim: Verstappen finished just one tenth of a second ahead of the penalised Antonelli at the end of the Miami sprint.

claims.quote: having been 0.631s slower than Bearman in that qualifying session, Ocon drove impeccably in the sprint, was the fastest Haas driver and mugged Bearman in the second half of the race to take 11th.
claims.claim: Ocon was 0.631 seconds slower than Bearman in sprint qualifying but outpaced him during the sprint race and overtook him in the second half to finish 11th.

claims.quote: Esteban Ocon entered this weekend with one point compared to Haas team-mate Ollie Bearman’s 17 scored in one fewer finish after Bearman’s massive Suzuka crash.
claims.claim: Heading into the Miami weekend, Ocon had scored one championship point while Bearman had scored 17 points from one fewer classified finish, following Bearman's crash at Suzuka.

claims.quote: Audi and Alpine were well up the road in the battle of the midfield and the team that came to Miami fourth in the constructors’ championship was painfully off the pace.
claims.claim: Haas arrived at Miami fourth in the constructors' championship but was significantly off the pace of Audi and Alpine in the midfield battle during the sprint.

docs.title: Winners and losers from F1 2026 Miami sprint qualifying

claims.quote: A first defeat of the season in a competitive session for Mercedes has to go down as a loss, even though championship leader Kimi Antonelli made the front row.
claims.claim: Miami sprint qualifying was Mercedes's first defeat of the 2026 season in a competitive session.

claims.quote: A comparison of Lando Norris's (at times scruffy) pole lap versus a relatively cleaner run from Antonelli, suggests nearly all the Mercedes time loss came through a slightly understeery run through Turn 1 and then a lack of pace through the high-speed sweeps thereafter.
claims.claim: Analysis of telemetry comparing Norris's pole lap to Antonelli's lap shows Mercedes lost most of its time at Turn 1 and through high-speed sections.

claims.quote: the speed traces also suggest - as in Suzuka - an initial divergence in terms of energy deployment strategy that seems to have once again given McLaren a Friday edge.
claims.claim: Speed trace data indicates McLaren had a different energy deployment strategy to Mercedes, giving McLaren an advantage in sprint qualifying.

claims.quote: Red Bull looks to have made a similar trade-off with deployment as Mercedes, so gaining on the runs to Turns 11 and 17 is offset against McLaren's superior speed heading to Turn 1 and between Turns 3 and 4.
claims.claim: Telemetry shows Red Bull made a similar energy deployment trade-off to Mercedes, gaining speed at Turns 11 and 17 but losing it at Turn 1 and between Turns 3 and 4 compared to McLaren.

claims.quote: The rest of that near-0.6s gap looks to be from the inferior speed Verstappen can carry through the corners. He loses a big chunk from Turns 4-8 and another whack though the fiddly bit of Turns 11-16.
claims.claim: Verstappen's lap was approximately 0.6 seconds off the pace, with corner speed losses concentrated in the Turns 4-8 and Turns 11-16 sections.

claims.quote: To be a second off \[Verstappen\], I don't know why - I've never been more than a tenth off so far this year when it mattered," he said
claims.claim: Hadjar stated he was approximately one second off Verstappen's pace in sprint qualifying, whereas previously he had never been more than a tenth off when it mattered.

claims.quote: Leclerc's 0.173s advantage over Oscar Piastri on medium Pirellis in SQ2 became a 0.370s deficit to Norris in SQ3
claims.claim: Leclerc was 0.173 seconds faster than Piastri in SQ2 on medium tyres but ended up 0.370 seconds slower than Norris in SQ3 on soft tyres.

claims.quote: Fastest in free practice, second fastest in SQ1 (only 0.010s away from the top) and fastest again in SQ2 (by nearly two tenths), Charles Leclerc was looking like the guy who was going to topple Mercedes in Miami.
claims.claim: Leclerc was fastest in free practice, second in SQ1 by 0.010s, and fastest in SQ2 by nearly two tenths of a second.

claims.quote: Aston Martin continued to prop up the order on a day where its best recorded laptime in sprint qualifying was slower than the worst F2 qualifying lap - and that series has never even been to Miami before.
claims.claim: Aston Martin's best sprint qualifying lap time was slower than the slowest lap recorded in the F2 qualifying session at Miami.

claims.quote: Fernando Alonso was over 10 seconds slower than the next slowest car, Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac, thanks to exceeding track limits in SQ1\. Alonso's best recorded lap - a 1m32.490s - wouldn't have placed him any better than 21st had it actually counted
claims.claim: Alonso's fastest recorded lap of 1m32.490s, which was deleted for track limits, was still only good enough for 21st place.

claims.quote: Lance Stroll didn't even set a time as he briefly stopped in the Turn 16 runoff after a big lock-up, and then returned to the pits with apparent brake issues.
claims.claim: Lance Stroll failed to set a timed lap in sprint qualifying after stopping in the Turn 16 runoff due to a lock-up and subsequent brake issues.

claims.quote: Carlos Sainz blasted his Williams team for being "three steps behind" on its execution, and lamented energy-deployment issues for halting any chance of an SQ3 push.
claims.claim: Carlos Sainz publicly criticised Williams's execution and said energy-deployment problems prevented him from challenging for SQ3.

claims.quote: Alex Albon said he was happy with the progress on the car and it felt like a genuine, deserved SQ2 appearance. But then it turned out he exceeded track limits on his best SQ1 lap and shouldn't have been in SQ2 at all.
claims.claim: Albon's best SQ1 lap was retrospectively deleted for a track limits violation, meaning he should not have progressed to SQ2.

claims.quote: Perez said of the "issues" that he'd experienced: "Basically we went out too late, and then we just didn't have enough time for refuelling and \[to\] go back \[out\] again
claims.claim: Perez said Cadillac's operational timing cost him a potential SQ2 appearance due to late deployment and insufficient time to refuel and re-exit.

claims.quote: a near-six-tenth advantage over Valtteri Bottas (that was consistent with his edge in FP1) is nothing to be sniffed at, nor is recording that after losing time to "issues with the engine" in practice.
claims.claim: Perez outpaced Bottas by close to six tenths of a second in sprint qualifying, a margin consistent with his advantage in FP1, despite engine issues in practice.

docs.title: STRATEGY GUIDE: What are the tactical options for the 2026 Miami Grand Prix?

claims.quote: Every race in Miami has seen a one-stop victory on the hard and medium tyres and, [Oscar Piastris](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/oscar-piastri) 2025 victory was no different. Piastri started P4, on a medium compound, climbed to P3 at the start, passed Kimi Antonelli for P2 on Lap 4 and passed [Max
claims.claim: Oscar Piastri won the 2025 Miami Grand Prix with a one-stop strategy on medium and hard tyres, starting P4, passing Antonelli for P2 on Lap 4 and Verstappen for the lead on Lap 14.

claims.quote: A Virtual Safety Car fell kindly for the leaders, with Piastri, [Lando Norris](https://www.formula1.com/en/drivers/lando-norris), George Russell and Charles Leclerc all making their pit-stop on Lap 28
claims.claim: A Virtual Safety Car occurred during the 2025 Miami Grand Prix, prompting Piastri, Norris, Russell and Leclerc to all pit on Lap 28.

claims.quote: Everybody who finished did a single stop, and nobody raced on a soft tyre. Of the cars that scored points, eight ran the medium>hard strategy, and made their stops between laps 25 and 29.
claims.claim: All finishers in the 2025 Miami Grand Prix made a single pit stop, no soft tyres were used, and eight points-scorers ran a medium-to-hard strategy stopping between laps 25 and 29.

claims.quote: The outliers were George Russell (P3) and Lewis Hamilton (P8) who went the other way with hard>medium strategy, both successfully making up ground on their starting positions  though both pitted under the VSC with the medium-shod runners
claims.claim: George Russell (P3) and Lewis Hamilton (P8) ran a hard-to-medium strategy in the 2025 Miami Grand Prix, gaining positions and pitting under the VSC.

claims.quote: The top 10 on the grid features two [Mercedes](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/mercedes), two Red Bulls, two Ferraris, two McLarens and two [Alpines](https://www.formula1.com/en/teams/alpine), which is exactly what we had in the top 10 finishing positions for the Sprint
claims.claim: The top 10 grid positions for the 2025 Miami Grand Prix race comprised two Mercedes, two Red Bulls, two Ferraris, two McLarens and two Alpines, mirroring the Sprint top-10 finishing order by constructor.

claims.quote: Given overtaking looked tricky on Saturday, there might be a benefit to trying a soft start to make early gains. The soft>hard is the likely route, and has an optimum stop window between Laps 16-22.
claims.claim: A soft-to-hard strategy for lower-grid starters has an optimal pit-stop window between laps 16 and 22 at the Miami Grand Prix.

claims.quote: The medium>soft race is also possible, and has a window between Laps 32-38.
claims.claim: A medium-to-soft strategy at the Miami Grand Prix has an optimal pit-stop window between laps 32 and 38.

claims.quote: There is a high probability of a Safety Car or VSC, and anyone deciding on medium>soft is obliged to stop in a narrow window that is not ideal. This is why I believe the hard tyre will play a big role in strategy
claims.claim: The analyst believes the hard tyre will play a significant role in the 2025 Miami Grand Prix strategy due to Safety Car likelihood and the narrow stop window imposed by a medium-to-soft strategy.

claims.quote: Our official forecast shows a front stalling across southern Florida, delivering a round of bad weather in the early morning, then a lull, and then a second, heavier, round arriving in the late afternoon, with the chance of rain increasing as the day progresses.
